color.why: G finds both landing palettes and text contrast restored, while M awards impeccable atmospheric light-spill credit; G also identifies impeccable’s static brass numeral (landing verdict G:13,29). On the app G measures both text palettes as compliant and Craft’s stronger input boundary, whereas M again favors impeccable’s light spill (app verdict G:26–28). Both instruction sets explicitly require measured contrast and semantic roles, so retain G’s ties rather than convert atmosphere into a new score.

craftRules.rule: Reuse project tokens and notation.
Measure the actual rendered foreground/background pair; change only when asked.
Input boundaries need 3:1 non-text contrast.

impRules.rule: Use semantic tokens and verify text, control and focus contrast in every state.
Color needs a stable role or world-specific atmospheric purpose.

instructionDepth.note: Craft is deeper on numeric ramps, semantic token grammar and measured-pair discipline; impeccable adds stronger atmosphere and page-scale color strategy.

color.variance: The shared identity supplied the palette; differences in light spill and input boundaries plausibly reflect execution and emphasis rather than missing contrast instructions.

typography.why: G calls both surfaces ties: both restore Geist roles, hierarchy and readable wrapping, with Craft’s app counts and file paths slightly better handled (landing verdict G:14; app verdict G:30–32). M favors impeccable on both surfaces, citing landing fact spacing and app casing, but its app claim of rigorous mono use conflicts with G’s specific sans counts/durations citations. Craft’s measured type rules and impeccable’s typeset guidance both cover the deciding mechanics; no blind winner survives the required margin under G.

craftRules.rule: Load every face and weight the design uses.
Pair each type role’s size, line-height and weight.
Balance headings, pretty-wrap prose and break escaping IDs.

impRules.rule: Run real copy at every breakpoint; maintain clear scale, weight and measure.
Use numeric, tabular, code and label features when content benefits.

instructionDepth.note: Craft has more explicit rendering, loading, punctuation, OpenType and input recipes; impeccable is deeper in assessing expressive role contrast and delivery as a whole.

typography.variance: Both provide adequate instructions; small wrapping, casing and role differences are more plausibly single-run execution than a demonstrated instructional advantage.

layout.why: Both judges favor impeccable’s landing composition; G specifically cites captioned samples in the first viewport and exposed mobile navigation (landing verdict G:15). App judges split: G favors Craft’s compact four-file list, current-room navigation and stacked mobile form, while M prefers impeccable’s featured render and compact band (app verdict G:34–36; M:65–68). Retain G’s source-supported app result, making equal-weight surface wins cancel.

craftRules.rule: Important content sits near the top; identifying content leads metadata/actions.
Keep expanded structure until content stops fitting, then collapse.
Hidden content needs a visible cue.

impRules.rule: Reject identical icon-heading-text cards as page structure.
Verify every supported viewport.
Make responsiveness structural.

instructionDepth.note: Craft is deeper on alignment, grouping, overflow and adaptation mechanics; impeccable is deeper on page composition, hierarchy and refusing generic scaffolds.

layout.variance: The landing scaffold difference fits impeccable’s explicit refusal rule; the app reversal exposes a composition-versus-scanability trade-off and substantial single-run variance.

accessibility.why: Both judges tie landing accessibility; G records clipped Craft nav focus and impeccable’s hidden comparison polarity, despite zero supplied axe violations (landing verdict G:16,46–53). On the app G favors Craft for preserved mobile names, a stronger field boundary, skip link, native modal and loading announcement; M’s generic tie misses named mobile controls disappearing with display:none (app verdict G:38–40,85–86). Craft’s detailed name, contrast and focus rules map directly to its app advantage, though impeccable also explicitly requires those checks.

craftRules.rule: Icon-only controls need descriptive names retaining visible text.
Prefer native dialog, move focus inside and restore the trigger.
UI boundaries require 3:1.

impRules.rule: Preserve visible focus, logical tab order, labels and appropriate targets.
Check screen-reader names, focus and semantics.
Icon-only controls need accessible names.

instructionDepth.note: Craft gives more implementation-level rules for names, focus, live regions, native semantics and exact WCAG distinctions; impeccable has broad audit and hardening coverage but less detail in its main polish route.

accessibility.variance: Craft’s depth is consistent with its app success, but impeccable’s missing names violate rules it already has, so this remains partly execution variance.

states.why: Both judges favor impeccable on both surfaces: landing has more visible clipboard status and intact focus, and app retry settles back to an error rather than remaining in loading (landing verdict G:17; app verdict G:42–44). Craft has a stronger native delete modal but its recovery deadlock, fixed four-render deletion count and incomplete loading geometry outweigh that local strength. Impeccable’s whole-path triage and connected recovery rule directly describe the advantage; Craft also forbids polishing over broken interactions, so the failure is not licensed by its rules.

craftRules.rule: Polish applies after interaction is sound and never outranks a broken interaction.
Inspect every defined state and disclose unrun checks.
Confirmation names consequence and counts where applicable.

impRules.rule: Fix blocked tasks and misleading state before missing states and visual polish.
Arrival, transition, empty and recovery paths must connect.
Every control needs appropriate state behavior.

instructionDepth.note: Craft is detailed on surfaces and the explicitly requested state workbench; impeccable more deeply integrates product-state lifecycles, recovery, triage and resilience across a complete path.

states.variance: The repeated win fits impeccable’s whole-path emphasis, but Craft’s retry deadlock is an execution failure despite applicable recovery and verification rules.

copy.why: G ties landing copy and both judges tie app copy: both replace false AI/pipeline claims with documented code-rendering and agent-ask facts (landing verdict G:18; app verdict G:46–48). M’s landing preference for impeccable’s dry humor is a voice judgment, not evidence Craft lacks writing instructions: Craft’s Copy mode IS upstream better-writing, verified in SOURCE-MANIFEST.json:442–469 and the copy entry’s name. Both prescribe product vocabulary, action-specific labels and recovery; both app outputs still claim saves/deletions without persistence, so this outcome does not establish a meaningful instruction difference.

craftRules.rule: A deliberate brand voice is not a defect; taste alone is not a finding.
Keep the product’s existing voice and vocabulary.
Buttons name actions and links name destinations.
Check labels against actual invoked actions.

impRules.rule: Preserve factual meaning, terminology and brand voice.
Action labels describe the actual outcome.
Success confirms a completed outcome.

instructionDepth.note: Craft’s better-writing is a full interface-copy method with inventory, voice, terminology, localization, confirmation and reporting detail; impeccable’s clarify is similarly capable but more compact.

copy.variance: The common factual recovery and blind ties support execution/voice variance, not a claim that one contestant had a writing skill and the other did not.

motion.why: Both judges favor impeccable landing motion; G cites Craft’s 500ms stagger and press scale under reduced motion versus impeccable’s restrained light/fades (landing verdict G:19,39). G favors impeccable app motion because its reduced-motion path stops skeleton sweeps and supplies continuity, while Craft’s spinner continues and views swap instantly; M calls that app margin a tie (app verdict G:50–52). Crucially, Craft explicitly keeps loading spinners under reduced motion and brief functional press feedback, so these are partly instruction-policy differences, not proof the contestant ignored atlas-motion; M’s retained fill-mode animation count is also not proof of perpetual visual movement.

craftRules.rule: Gate motion by frequency and named purpose.
Reduced motion keeps opacity/color and removes movement.
Reduced-motion guidance explicitly keeps loading spinners and brief functional press feedback.
Bundled UI fallback keeps opacity and gates movement, scale and blur.
Shared Animate owner overrides UI recipe presets.

impRules.rule: A generic fade-and-rise is not a product-specific motion thesis.
Every animation needs an intentional reduced-motion path.
One authored moment from an already-visible default.
Do not add animation just to make polish visible.

instructionDepth.note: Team Craft means atlas-motion plus bundled Craft refs: it is deeper on frequency gates, timing, interruption, gesture physics and performance; impeccable is more flexible and explicit on authored material and continuity.

motion.variance: Impeccable’s landing advantage fits its product-specific thesis; the app spinner difference is partly traceable to Craft’s permissive exception, while choreography choices remain single-run execution.

ux.why: Both judges favor impeccable landing UX: captioned work appears earlier and the command action is literal, whereas Craft’s Start the Desk only scrolls (landing verdict G:20). G ties the app: impeccable leads with the latest render and Craft keeps scanability, current-room navigation and a general ask action, each with material defects (app verdict G:54–56). Impeccable explicitly distinguishes Persuade from Operate and requires a working opening action; Craft preserves identity and prioritizes content but has no comparable end-to-end direction method.

craftRules.rule: Preserve accepted identity; a new direction needs its own decision.
Give each view one primary action.
Put important content near the top.

impRules.rule: Persuade opening makes the offer clear, shows a working action and product-specific proof.
Operate prioritizes task scanability and consistency.
Make primary task and current state obvious.

instructionDepth.note: Craft gives strong local refinement and identity boundaries; impeccable is substantially deeper on surface purpose, product truth, concept generation, visitor path, direction contracts and finishing.

ux.variance: The landing win is plausibly instruction-led through Persuade’s real-action requirement, but the app tie prevents generalizing this run into universal UX superiority.

craft.behavior: Declined new-direction construction, also declined an unwanted tidy-up, and left index.html byte-identical to seeds/landing.orig/index.html (cmp verified). The supplied 390px metrics retain 1180px scroll width and the original accessibility/motion defects.
craft.contractAdherence: Consistent with its narrow refinement contract and absence of a direction-selection method. SKILL.md:23 reserves a separate direction decision; it does not literally say never redesign or refuse a user who has already requested one, so the all-stop is a conservative benchmark interpretation reinforced by the ban on substituting general design knowledge, not a universal hard prohibition. Notes cite stale line 22; current verified line is 23.

imp.behavior: Built a replacement Three-Drum Riso Zine: full blue opening, pink/yellow ink vocabulary, Bricolage display, misregistration, textured floods, live deterministic canvas, Play/Pause, frame scrubber and drum toggles. Added inferred PRODUCT.md, six-block surface contract, token-bearing landing DESIGN.md and JSON sidecar.
imp.quality: Clear direction capability win: supplied desktop/mobile views show a distinctive, legible code-rendering demonstration and a visible command action. Source verifies multiply compositing, seeded dropout, frame controls, paused reduced-motion default and offscreen/hidden drawing guard; supplied metrics have no page overflow at 1440/390 and zero axe findings. This is screenshot/source judgment, not fresh runtime interaction or a claim of production readiness.
imp.contractAdherence: Substantially follows replacement-world, concept seed, contract and documentation instructions, but not fully: NOTES:54 says decision wait exited 3 and the build proceeded, whereas new-work.md:51 requires repeating exit 3 and reserves the unanswered fallback for exit 4. NOTES:25–27 describe inferred PRODUCT.md before the later decision-page attempt; init.md:31 requires probing an available decision page before inference. Review remains self-reported fix with one partial item, honestly disclosed rather than passed; scoped landing documentation preserves the Desk’s separate root system.
imp.risks: The supplied full-page screenshot still shows paper in the intended yellow creations and pink Desk regions, consistent with the reported open print-in issue; source’s awaiting cover depends on IntersectionObserver firing. Product audience and CTA remain inferred; pnpm desk:start precedes prerequisites. Clipboard failure only says Press ⌘C and has no live status region; the reduced-motion preference is read at startup rather than updated. A conventional copy-left/canvas-right hero limits how radical the composition is, even though the material and live mechanism are specific.

direction.verdict: Impeccable wins direction task completion and demonstrated direction quality; Craft is out of scope / no submission, not a poor redesign. For an end-to-end direction-capability score count Craft as unfulfilled (zero completion), while any quality-only comparison marks Craft N/A and reports impeccable alone; report Craft’s scope adherence separately. Do not average this asymmetric scope test into the eight refinement pillars or excuse impeccable’s process deviations and open fix disposition.

refusals.what: New visual direction needs a separate decision; no direction-creation method is supplied.
Whole-interface audits/change reviews route to Atlas Review; substantial prose routes to Writing for Humans.
Domain handoffs do not require cross-discipline orchestration for ordinary refinement.
States creates a workbench only on explicit request; ordinary state polish does not authorize rebuilding the Bench or removing it.
Contrast or palette changes require authorization; the refinement briefs already authorize these fixes.
Do not introduce a new face unless asked for a type change.
Ask between the two visually different iOS 16px input fixes; app contestant chose sizing up under non-interactive constraints.
Reject animation failing frequency or purpose gates; this is a successful refusal, not a missing effect.
Motion Opportunities is read-only, Performance diagnoses first, audits/reviews route to Atlas Review; React Native/Expo is excluded.
Refinement preserves identity/behavior; redesign replaces the world but preserves product truth.
Ask before replacing factual copy or adding claims; supplied refinement facts and non-interactive constraints explain the disclosed substitutions.
Polish must not conceal redesign; if the concept is wrong route to redesign or bolder.
Audit reports and does not fix; web audit routes native platforms elsewhere.
A new identity found during colorizing or typesetting routes through new-work rather than local refinement.
Missing PRODUCT blocks new/replacement work through init, but narrow existing refinements may proceed and offer init afterward.
Local extensions inherit identity and need approval before durable DESIGN.md changes.
Direction selection must run concept-seed and follow the decision-page answer/fallback contract; no silent skip.
No image generation means code-led, not a refused build; code-led skips comp round by contract.
Do not fabricate factual/commercial claims or unsupported capabilities.
Do not repair context drift as a design-task side effect.
Default scaffolds are refused; eyebrows are an absolute ban, while most other defaults can be earned by the brief.

overall: On equal-weight refinement surfaces, color, typography, layout and copy tie; Craft wins accessibility, and impeccable wins states, motion and UX. G is preferred on disagreements because its evidence is more discriminating, while M marks every plant fixed and sometimes contradicts its own defects. Craft’s deeper mechanical instructions do not guarantee cleaner execution, and its Copy mode is better-writing. Impeccable alone demonstrates replacement-direction capability, with an open fix disposition and documented process deviations. These single runs establish observed outcomes and plausible rule links, not causal proof or a population-level ranking.
